passage: Some scientists argue that octopuses' skill at solving puzzles shows an intelligence comparable to that of many mammals. Others caution that the octopus nervous system is organized so differently, with most of its neurons located in its arms rather than its brain, that such comparisons may be misleading. For these researchers, the more useful question is not how intelligent octopuses are compared with mammals but how their unusual nervous system produces such flexible behavior.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Some researchers argue that octopus intelligence should be studied on its own terms rather than compared with mammals'.
Octopuses have been shown to be more intelligent than all mammals because they can solve puzzles that mammals cannot.
Most of an animal's neurons are located in its brain, which is why octopuses are less intelligent than most mammals.
Octopuses cannot solve puzzles without help from researchers, so their intelligence has been greatly overestimated.
steps: The text presents two views: one compares octopuses with mammals; the other cautions against it.
The text ends with the second group's preferred question: how the octopus's own system produces flexible behavior.
So the central idea is the call to study octopus intelligence on its own terms.
The text doesn't rank octopuses above mammals, says octopus neurons are mostly in the arms, and describes octopuses solving puzzles.
key: When a text presents two views and ends by developing one, that view is usually the focus.
